verdicts.matching_evidence: The relation "g = 2eα" is dimensionally and physically incorrect. The Dirac quantization condition reads g·e = nħ/2, i.e. g_D = ħc/(2e) in Gaussian units, which equals e/(2α) ≈ 68.5 e — not 2eα. The numerical value 3.3×10⁻⁸ esu, however, *is* approximately correct for the Dirac charge... The formula "g = 2eα" written next to the correct numerical value is therefore a factor-of-(4α²) ~ 2×10⁻⁴ algebraic error in the symbolic expression even though the printed number is right. This is almost certainly a typo for "g = e/(2α)".
